links.comparator_used: Label-only output without a required verbatim supporting quote (abstention allowed in both conditions)
links.outcome: Macro-F1 and coverage (non-invalid, non-abstained outputs) for trial eligibility-scope classification
links.effect: Coverage fell: GPT-5.2 86.2% to 84.3%, Gemini 3 flash preview 98.3% to 92.8%, Claude Opus 4.5 96.0% to 94.5%. Macro-F1 stayed high, with slight gains for GPT-5.2 and Gemini and a decrease for Claude. Labels were stable across repetitions (Fleiss' kappa 0.829 to 0.969).
links.tradeoff: Coverage dropped because of more abstentions and, for Gemini, more invalid outputs. Only 48.0% to 78.8% of evidence-bearing predictions were judged semantically supported, so the approach introduces new failure modes.
links.quote: Macro-F1 remained high but changed by model (slight gains for GPT-5.2 and Gemini, decrease for Claude).

links.comparator_used: All predictions released without filtering on whether the quote supports the label
links.outcome: Macro-F1 when restricted to predictions whose quote was verified (mechanically as an exact substring and by LLM judge as supporting the label)
links.effect: Restricting to supported predictions increased macro-F1; no numbers were given in the abstract.
links.tradeoff: Lower coverage. Mechanically valid quotes occurred in 83.3% to 91.2% of runs, but only 48.0% to 78.8% of evidence-bearing predictions were judged semantically supported.
links.quote: Restricting to supported predictions increased macro-F1 at the cost of lower coverage.

design_hint: verbatim quote evidence requirement and mechanical validation
